topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students and introduces the course context, central questions, and learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Genesis: Genetics, Microenvironment, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by endogenous processes, environmental mutagens, and geographical epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, using the detailed historical and mechanistic case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogens, Promoters, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which specific chemical mutagens, radiation, tumor promoters, and host developmental stages contribute to carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the experimental and population-level methods—including mutational signatures, epidemiology, animal models, and the Ames test—used to establish and evaluate carcinogenic risks.
